title: How can a very long number be written without miscounting zeroes?
description: The book's big facts, such as the Sun's distance from the centre of the galaxy, have so many zeroes that we may miscount them. The point is moved to leave one digit in front, and the number of places moved becomes the power of ten. Keeko doubts that fifty nine times ten squared is also scientific notation.
teaching_notes: One idea: scientific notation keeps a number from one up to ten in front and lets the power of ten count the places. Watch for students who leave two digits in front and still call it scientific notation.

source: Write 5900 in four ways using powers of 10, and write the th
video_script.why: Very long numbers are hard to read. Moving the point to leave one digit in front makes the power of ten do the counting.
video_script.substitution: Move the point until one digit is in front, count the places moved, and use the count as the power of ten.
video_script.anchor: 5900 written four ways, then the three large facts from the book
video_script.wrong_answer: fifty nine times ten squared is scientific notation too
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks any number times a power of ten is scientific notation. The number in front must be at least one and less than ten.
video_script.payoff_line: The power of ten counts the places the point has moved

final_answer.value: 5900 = 5.9 × 10³; 3 × 10 to the power 20 m; 1 × 10 to the power 11; 5.976 × 10 to the power 24 kg
final_answer.spoken: five point nine times ten cubed, three times ten to the power twenty metres, one times ten to the power eleven, and five point nine seven six times ten to the power twenty four kilograms

maths_rules: only 5.9 × 10³ has a number from 1 up to (not including) 10 in front
59,76 followed by 21 zeroes has 25 digits, so the point moves 24 places: 5.976 × 10²⁴
the slip: 59 × 10² = 5900 is true, but 59 is not less than 10
video_script.design: The four forms of 5900 stay in the working area as a ladder. The three facts come one at a time, each with its point-moving arrow.

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Here is five thousand nine hundred, written in four ways.
Five hundred ninety times ten, and fifty nine times ten squared.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Then five point nine times ten cubed, and zero point five nine times ten to the power four.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Only one of these has a number at least one and less than ten in front.
Writing a number that way is called scientific notation.

<bookmark mark='ans1'/>Five thousand nine hundred is five point nine times ten cubed.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The Sun is three times ten to the power twenty metres away.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks fifty nine times ten squared is scientific notation too.
